intervention_identity: clemastine fumarate (ChEMBL CHEMBL1200795; parent CHEMBL1626; max phase 4, approved antihistamine)
action: M1 muscarinic receptor antagonist (ChEMBL action: ANTAGONIST on M1) acting on OPCs in the precedent; also an H1 antagonist, so which receptor carries a myelin effect is a separate question
context_where_shown: adult relapsing MS with chronic demyelinating optic neuropathy; neonatal hypoxic white-matter injury and preterm white-matter injury in mouse
other_disease_precedent_NOT_WWOX_evidenc: ReBUILD, PMID 29029896: primary endpoint met, P100 latency shortened 1.7 ms/eye (95% CI 0.5-2.9, p=0.0048), crossover, 50 patients, fatigue reported, no serious AEs; Cree 2018 Brain PMID 29244098: neonatal hypoxia mouse, OPC differentiation, myelination, functional recovery via M1 on OPCs; Odell 2024 PMID 38942888: mouse minimum effective dose, pharmacokinetics
WWOX_system_evidence: none: no WWOX-deficient system has received any myelin-directed compound (card F02 abstention)
transferability_hypothesis_labelled_IPOT: IPOTESI: the OPC differentiation block seen in WWOX-deficient systems (E02, E09, E23) is M1-sensitive and downstream of a missing neuronal signal, so a receptor-level push on OPCs can bypass it; the preprint shows an OPC-intrinsic delay, which would make a bypass more plausible, but the in vivo baseline O-KO shows no hypomyelination, which would make it less informative
hypothesised_benefit: none claimed; the hypothesis is only that a stalled OPC population can be moved; whether more myelin means a functional gain (conduction, seizures, development) is unproven in any WWOX system and, in ReBUILD, rested on a surrogate
discriminating_test_as_question: Does clemastine shift wild-type OPCs on Wwox-null DRG neurons from pre-myelinating to myelinating MBP+ morphology, and does it do so in Wwox-null OPC monoculture, with total MBP+ cell number reported beside the ratio?
contrast: drug versus vehicle in KO-DRG + WT-OPC, against the same contrast in WT-DRG + WT-OPC (interaction), and a genetic arm (Chrm1-deficient OPCs) to attribute the effect to M1 rather than H1
falsification: no shift in the KO-DRG arm, or an equal shift in the WT-DRG arm (generic differentiation push, not a rescue of the WWOX-dependent defect), or an effect that persists in Chrm1-deficient OPCs (an M1-independent action, e.g. H1 or off-target); also a ratio shift accompanied by fewer total MBP+ cells (selective loss, not maturation)
known_context_flags_for_this_genotype: first-generation H1 antihistamine with anticholinergic and sedative actions: seizure-threshold and sedation questions in a seizure-prone infant brain are unmeasured; label lookup NOT_ATTEMPTED; Wwox-null mice are hypoglycaemic and die early so in vivo testing has a narrow window; OPC expression of Chrm1 in Wwox-deficient cells not measured
reading_depth_of_precedent: abstract level (Europe PMC records 2026-10-31); papers not read in full
verdict: RESTRICT: pertinent as an in-vitro question only; not a candidate for the ranking

intervention_identity: benztropine mesylate (ChEMBL CHEMBL1200383; max phase 4; approved anticholinergic)
action: muscarinic M1/M3 antagonist in the precedent (Deshmukh 2013 abstract); ChEMBL mechanism row not retrieved for this id
context_where_shown: in vitro OPC differentiation screen; mouse EAE and cuprizone
other_disease_precedent_NOT_WWOX_evidenc: Deshmukh 2013 Nature PMID 24107995: preclinical only (rat OPC screen, mouse EAE, cuprizone); no randomised myelin trial retrieved here
transferability_hypothesis_labelled_IPOT: IPOTESI as C1; used as a class comparator, not as independent support: evidence for one muscarinic antagonist is not transferred to the other (no transfer between molecules)
discriminating_test_as_question: same assay as C1 as a second compound with no H1 component, to ask whether the myelin-maturation effect follows muscarinic antagonism
contrast: benztropine versus clemastine in the same KO-DRG/WT-DRG design
falsification: concordance with clemastine is not independent replication of a WWOX effect (shared target class); discordance means the clemastine effect is H1 or off-target
known_context_flags_for_this_genotype: anticholinergic burden, dopamine-transporter inhibition; seizure and paediatric exposure data not retrieved

intervention_identity: bexarotene (ChEMBL CHEMBL1023; max phase 4, approved for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma)
other_disease_precedent_NOT_WWOX_evidenc: CCMR One, Lancet Neurol 2021 PMID 34418398: primary efficacy (lesional MTR) NOT met (adjusted difference 0.16 pu, 95% CI -0.39 to 0.71, p=0.55); every bexarotene-treated participant had an adverse event, central hypothyroidism 26/26, hypertriglyceridaemia 24/26; authors do not recommend use
falsification: a negative primary efficacy result and poor tolerability in the one human trial retrieved
known_context_flags_for_this_genotype: hypothyroidism and lipid effects, plus teratogenicity, in a developing brain
verdict: DO NOT ADVANCE: negative human precedent; no WWOX rationale

action: AMPK-related metabolic rejuvenation of aged OPCs in the precedent
context_where_shown: aged rodent OPCs and focal demyelination in aged mice
other_disease_precedent_NOT_WWOX_evidenc: Neumann 2019 Cell Stem Cell PMID 31585093: restores differentiation of aged OPCs; the benefit is age-related, no developmental precedent retrieved
WWOX_system_evidence: none; the preprint notes lower oxidative-phosphorylation programmes in null OPC cultures (E23), not a drug effect
transferability_hypothesis_labelled_IPOT: IPOTESI: a metabolic deficit in Wwox-null OPCs is a lever; unsupported by any measurement of OPC metabolism beyond transcript pathway scores
known_context_flags_for_this_genotype: Wwox-null mice are hypoglycaemic (module record); a glucose-lowering agent in that context needs its own safety question; paediatric exposure not assessed
verdict: DO NOT ADVANCE: age mismatch (aged versus developing OPCs) and a glycaemia flag; reopen only if null-OPC metabolism is measured

intervention_identity: WNT-pathway restraint via tankyrase/AXIN stabilisation (research compound XAV939, ChEMBL CHEMBL2431805, no approved product; class card D02)
action: stabilises AXIN2 and lowers beta-catenin signalling; in the precedent it promotes OPC maturation and remyelination
context_where_shown: neonatal hypoxia-ischaemia and cuprizone mouse models
other_disease_precedent_NOT_WWOX_evidenc: Fancy 2011 Nat Neurosci PMID 21706018 (abstract): AXIN2 expressed in immature OLPs in human newborn lesions; XAV939 in the mouse remyelination model
WWOX_system_evidence: none: the preprint shows WNT/TGF-beta gene enrichment in null OPCs (transcripts, E23, E27), not WNT pathway activity at the protein level
transferability_hypothesis_labelled_IPOT: IPOTESI: WWOX loss de-represses WNT in OPCs and that restrains differentiation; the sign of WNT change in WWOX-deficient neural tissue is contested elsewhere in the module (card D02, DL-MOL-003)
discriminating_test_as_question: Is beta-catenin transcriptional activity (reporter or target protein) higher in null than WT OPCs, before any inhibitor is considered?
contrast: null versus WT OPC, reporter read-out, with and without a genetic AXIN2/dominant-negative TCF arm
falsification: no difference in WNT activity at protein or reporter level makes the transcript enrichment non-causal
known_context_flags_for_this_genotype: a research compound with no paediatric or CNS exposure data; tankyrase inhibitors have wide pathway effects
verdict: HOLD: a mechanism read-out question, no compound entry

intervention_identity: genetic or pharmacological stabilisation of SOX10 (no specific compound; proteasome inhibition rescues SOX10 level in the preprint cell line only; class card A02)
action: WWOX WW1 domain binds SOX10 (PPxY) and reduces its proteasomal turnover in the preprint
context_where_shown: Oli-neu cells, primary OPC and remyelination mouse
transferability_hypothesis_labelled_IPOT: IPOTESI: the WWOX-SOX10 axis explains the OPC-intrinsic delay in WWOX-deficient OPCs
discriminating_test_as_question: Does SOX10 protein fall in null OPCs in vivo during development, and does restoring SOX10 alone rescue the differentiation delay?
contrast: SOX10 add-back in null OPC monoculture versus WWOX add-back
falsification: SOX10 add-back fails to rescue, or SOX10 protein is unchanged in developing OPCs
known_context_flags_for_this_genotype: proteasome inhibitors are toxic and not a chronic paediatric option; the interaction is unreplicated
